description_full: Dycom Industries, Inc. provides specialty contracting services to the digital infrastructure, telecommunications infrastructure, and utility industries in the United States. It operates through Communications and Building Systems segments. The company offers engineering services to telecommunications providers, including the planning and design of aerial, underground, and buried fiber optic, copper, and coaxial cable systems; placement of cables, related structures, and drop lines for telephone companies and cable multiple system operators; program and project management, and inspection personnel; and wireless networks in connection with the deployment of macro cell and new small cell sites. It also provides construction, maintenance, and installation services, such as placement and splicing of copper, fiber, and coaxial cables; tower construction, lines and antenna installation, foundation and equipment pad construction, and small cell site placement for wireless carriers, as well as equipment installation and material fabrication, and site testing services; underground facility locating services, including locating telephone, cable television, power, water, sewer, and gas lines for utility companies; installation and maintenance of customer premise equipment for electric and gas utilities, and other customers. Dycom Industries, Inc. was incorporated in 1969 and is based in West Palm Beach, Florida.

financial_summary: Dycom Industries, Inc. is a mid-cap industrials business with a $6.7B market cap on $5.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +13% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $402M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.28× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 5.9×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.5%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
